task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
How much the offense reorganizes (relative to L) predicts the change in points per possession.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=986; n=148, mde rho; 148 spells

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

failed_approaches.why: A_unanswerable due to insufficient scoreable instances; sample size too small (n=8) and design unanswerable
C_artifact: apparent effect inflated by low‑n leaders; small sample distortion

evidence_does_not_establish: No prior study directly examined how offensive reorganization after a player absence predicts changes in points per possession; existing studies were limited by small samples or were untestable.
own_inferences: The available dataset contains 986 observations and 148 spells, suggesting that many lineup changes are rare and the data may be sparse for robust estimation of reorganization effects. The presence of small‑sample artifacts in prior work signals a risk of over‑estimating effects when few possessions are available per spell.
uncertainties: Exact definition of “offensive reorganization” and how it is measured in [source] database; the granularity of lineup spell identification; potential unobserved confounders such as opponent defensive adjustments.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records did not address the specific research question, so they do not alter the assessment of feasibility.

blocking_constraints.text: Only a fraction of lineup changes have enough possessions to estimate a reliable points‑per‑possession change
Many player absences are infrequent, leading to sparse exposure for reorganization metrics
Opponent defensive adjustments and game context may bias observed changes

prior_work.summary: No prior study directly addressed the causal link between offensive reorganization following a player absence and points per possession; existing literature focused on trigger timing, routing, or absence validation, all limited by small samples or methodological constraints.

risks.text: Insufficient number of possessions per spell to estimate effects with adequate power
Player absences and resulting lineup changes are rare, limiting the number of observations
Unclear reliability of the reorganization metric derived from graph‑based possession records
Opponent defensive strategy and game state may confound observed points‑per‑possession changes

design.estimand: difference in points per possession before and after offensive reorganization following a player absence
design.sample: all observed spells with at least 10 possessions pre‑ and post‑absence
design.power: not sufficient to reliably detect small effects; power < 0.4 for realistic effect sizes
design.controls: include game context, opponent defensive rating, and period of the game
design.falsification: compare to spells where no player absence occurred but similar lineup changes happen (e.g., voluntary substitutions)
design.multiplicity: control for multiple lineup spells per team by using cluster‑robust standard errors
design.decision_rule: reject null if p<0.05 after adjustment for clustering
design.data_version: NBA 2022‑23 to 2025‑26 seasons, per‑game play‑by‑play derived graph database
